mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it signals an overheating labor market that triggers aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 3.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY) and rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) signal an aggressive monetary policy response, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals an economic contraction phase, reducing corporate earnings growth and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS above 3-month moving average) indicate robust consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS exceeds its 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: Excessive job growth (PAYEMS > 200,000 monthly) signals labor market overheating that may trigger inflationary pressures and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 200000, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4.0% YoY) combined with weak housing starts (HOUST < 1400) indicates stagflationary pressures where monetary policy is constrained, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 4.0% and HOUST < 1400, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate < 1.0%) signals an economic deceleration phase, reducing corporate profit expectations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 annualized growth rate < 1.0%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
